narration: Your bank says refi and save two hundred bucks a month. Sounds like a win, right? But here's what they conveniently left out of that pitch.
visual: A house SVG springs onto screen. A green 'SAVE $200/MO' badge bounces in below it. A red warning triangle springs up. Text: 'THE REFINANCE TRAP'.

narration: Every refinance hits you with closing costs — usually five to six thousand dollars in fees. That money's gone on day one, before you save a single cent.
visual: A white receipt card slides in on dark background. Line items animate in one by one: Loan Origination $2,100, Appraisal $600, Title Insurance $1,800, Other Fees $1,500. Total: $6,000 in red.

narration: Here's the math nobody runs for you. Closing costs divided by monthly savings equals your break-even date. Six thousand divided by two hundred is thirty months — two and a half years.
visual: An equation box shows '$6,000 ÷ $200' on warm background. A large '30 MONTHS' springs in below it. A red progress bar fills left to right representing the timeline.

narration: Here's the wild part. Fifty-two percent of homeowners move within five years of refinancing. That's more than half who never even reach their break-even date.
visual: A house with a red SOLD sign and a moving truck SVG appear side by side on dark background. A large '52%' stat springs into view below them.

narration: Sell before month thirty and your six thousand in closing costs just vanished — with nothing to show. Refinanced twice in five years? You could be down eighteen thousand dollars.
visual: A piggy bank SVG tilts and tips on light background. A '-$18,000' counter counts down in red. A small bar chart drops below zero. Badge: '$18K GONE — NOTHING BACK'.

narration: Run the break-even math first. If there's any chance you'll move before you hit that number, don't touch your rate. The lower payment only wins if you're there to collect it.
visual: Three numbered checklist items spring in on dark background: 1. Calculate break-even date, 2. Compare to move timeline, 3. Only refi if you'll stay past it. A red formula box. CTA text.
